quotes.text: Folder first thinking assumes humans remember paths. They don't. No metadata means no beacons. Broken inheritance leaks permissions down forgotten warrants.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one breath why folder-based document management fails audits.

quotes.text: A label without enforcement is a banner in the wind. We tie it to encryption and policy so it defends, not decorates.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable argument that sensitivity labels only matter when bound to encryption and policy.

quotes.text: We start in simulation mode. We learn the traffic. We tune the rules. Then we enforce. With user tips and justified overrides, where business demands speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, actionable rollout pattern for DLP policies without breaking operations.

quotes.text: Governance is not a project, it's crew discipline, we schedule drills, we verify seals, we adjust fire
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames compliance governance as an ongoing operating routine rather than a one-time project.

quotes.text: Before we arm co-pilot's, we hard seal data boundaries. Block AI from learning on restricted and confidential unless explicitly allowed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete recommendation to secure data boundaries before rolling out Copilot.

chapters.title: Red alert: building an audit-ready ECM
The problem: document chaos and audit failures
The imperial archive pattern: sites, libraries, content types and metadata
Law and order: sensitivity labels, retention and DLP
The audit crucible: eDiscovery and compliance monitoring
Maintenance and future readiness: governance as crew discipline

takeaways: Replace folder sprawl with a fortress pattern: one site per mission, one library per vault, central content types and a small set of required metadata.
Sensitivity labels, retention labels and DLP only protect content when they are tied to encryption and enforcement, rolled out in simulation first and scoped by admin units.
Audit readiness comes from routine: pre-staged eDiscovery templates, Compliance Manager evidence, access reviews and a recurring governance sprint.
hook: When a regulator asks for the approved, redacted contract with full lineage, most Microsoft 365 tenants drown in folders and duplicate versions. This episode is for admins and compliance leads who want SharePoint and Microsoft Purview to work as one defense system. You get a practical runbook for labels, DLP, retention and eDiscovery that makes a five-minute audit realistic.
